text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as oil prices weakened and refining margins came under pressure. US crude is trading at $82.24 per barrel—down sharply from levels earlier this month—while refineries are running at a high 97.5% capacity, which means refining companies have less room to boost output or margins when demand softens. The gap between crude costs and refined product values (what refiners actually earn) tightens when oil prices fall but storage levels stay elevated: gasoline and diesel inventories remain above seasonal norms, suggesting demand isn't keeping pace with supply.

The broader context is a shift in energy sentiment. While climate talks in Geneva collapsed on fossil fuel language over the weekend—which might normally support oil prices—the market is instead pricing in a longer-term softening as AI-driven energy infrastructure investment in Latin America and elsewhere remains contingent on actual infrastructure buildout, not just potential. Near-term refining economics are simply weaker right now, and that's what's driving the stock down.
